title: Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the intelligibility in context scale for Azerbaijani Turkish-speaking children
abstract: This study aimed to cross-culturally adapt the Intelligibility in Context Scale (ICS) into Azerbaijani Turkish (ICS-AZ) and evaluate its psychometric properties. Following forward-backward translation and expert review ( = 13 SLPs), the ICS-AZ was completed by parents of 180 children (3-5 years: 40 with speech sound disorders (SSD) and 140 typically developing (TD) peers). Assessments included Percentage of Consonant Correct (PCC), Phonological Mean Length of Utterance (PMLU), Whole-Word Proximity (PWP), and Proportion of Whole-Word Correctness (PWC). Content, construct, convergent, discriminant validity, internal consistency, and test-retest reliability were examined. Exploratory factor analyses supported a robust unidimensional structure across mother (loadings: 0.77-0.95) and father forms (loadings: 0.86-0.98). Known-groups validity demonstrated significant differences between SSD and TD groups, yielding very large effect sizes for mother (Cohen's d = 2.57) and father ratings (Cohen's d = 2.39). Convergent validity was supported by strong positive correlations with PCC ( = .71-.72), PMLU ( = .63-.68), PWP ( = .62-.67), and PWC ( = .62-.67, Spearman's= .617-.667; all< .001). Significant convergent correlations were found with PCC, PMLU, and whole-word measures. Additionally, the ICS-AZ exhibited excellent internal consistency ( = 0.97-0.98) and test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.98). A cutoff score of ≤3.93 demonstrated favorable diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity: 77.5%, specificity: 97.9%, positive predictive value: 91.2%, and negative predictive value of 93.8%. These findings confirm that the ICS-AZ is a valid, reliable, and clinically precise screening tool for assessing speech intelligibility in Azerbaijani Turkish-speaking preschool children.
